Daily Devotional

October 24

12 For it is a shame even to speak of those things which are done of them in secret. 13 But all things that are reproved are made manifest by the light: for whatsoever doth make manifest is light. - Eph 5:12-13 (KJV)

Paul has been teaching Christians to not indulge in ungodly acts, as they now are born again, and should no longer ever do those things (Ephesians 5:3-11). Now he is saying that we should not even speak of those ungodly things that people do in secret, but many Christians think they need to know all about the world’s trash, and get into all the gory details of what the heathens do. We should be aware that non-believers are committing evil deeds, but we should not talk about it with others, and we should not have to know the details of all the ungodly things that people do (1 Corinthians 15:33). It is of no benefit to dwell on the evil actions of people, but we should just reject them from our lives, and try to convert the sinners that do them. We are not sin police, looking for the people that do the ungodly acts, but should pray for them, and try to bring them to Christ with the Gospel.

When we live for Christ, and let our light shine in this dark world, we need to let people know that it is Christ living in us that makes us act like Him (Matthew 5:16). Just living a good life is not enough, if we don’t give God the credit for leading us to live that way. Remember that it is not about us, and how we shine our light, but it is all about Jesus, whose light we are shinning. Give credit to God for all your good actions, and make known the fact that everything good comes from above (James 1:17), giving glory to the Father. Be doers of the Word, and not just hearers (James 1:22), but give the glory to God – praise Him for all our blessings.

My biggest issue with Europe is that I think most of it (even the nice, rich parts) still carries baggage from its history that results in a truly class based view of the world and society. This does not mean aristocrats are subject to different de jure rules than peasants, but it does mean the very view of a man's relationship to society is colored by the assumption man is subservient to the collective.

Whatever the disfunctions of progressivism and long term racism (including the lingering effects of slavery), the American system is more to my liking. Unlike anyplace in Europe, it is not tied to millennia old culture. It may have heavily borrowed from its parent culture, but being set up on a foreign continent with a mix of citizens and a society not truly organically grown, but somewhat artificially constructed based in political theory currents from the Enlightenment means it is much better suited to the view that government does not exist outside and above the individuals in a society and the primary unit is the individual for many matters and the family for others.

Obviously, my views are somewhat idealistic and are not completely supported by all aspects of society in either the US or Europe, but foundationally, I believe the ideals are true and do exist.
